chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "It is disliked to combine two surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the voluntary prayer, there is no harm."
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine two surahs in one rak'ah of prayer?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) distinguishes between obligatory and voluntary prayers, ruling that combining two surahs in a single rak'ah is disliked (makruh) in fard prayers to preserve the distinct recitation structure, whereas it is permissible in nafl prayers. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the integrity of the Quranic recitation during the primary acts of worship while allowing flexibility in supererogatory acts. The distinction underscores the principle that obligatory acts require stricter adherence to prophetic precedent, while voluntary acts allow for broader permissibility.
